rationale: unit:shared.example.copy_field uses the grammar in shared.syntax and path behavior in shared.give. The exact sharing_execution proposition starts at State.empty with sharingCode and ends at twiceCopiedState with empty remaining code. I inspected those named definitions and intermediate step statements in context:lean/Shared/Examples.lean: Token(0) enters t; Box(1) receives its unique field and empties t; giveShare clears b and puts a shared Box reference in s without altering the unique Token field. The next field give changes that field to shared and adds u; the final give adds v while preserving it. twiceCopiedState has exactly the two objects, three shared Token occurrences (field,u,v), shared s, and empty t,b. Thus the example checks its stated complete setup and final ownership counts, including the distinction between sharing the container and later changing the field reference.
limitations: This comparison checks prose/notation and formal statement correspondence; it does not independently certify Lean proof checking or audit proof tactics.
